proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: register Mimikyu's ordinary/Busted forms and a saved once-per-battle disguise flag. A miss, immunity, weather tick, or tile hazard does not spend the disguise. Resolve ordinary eligible secondary effects after the disguise breaks; subsequent hits use normal damage. The flag never resets through healing or ability reacquisition. Confusion requires a separate authored status system before its self-hit can participate. Show the prevention and self-damage separately in previews and logs; restore ordinary form after battle.

proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: At initial deployment, sum the effective Defense and Special Defense of all living opponents after intrinsic rank, current stages, and continuous modifiers. If summed Defense is strictly lower, grant the holder +1 Attack; otherwise grant +1 Special Attack, including ties. Apply the selected stage once per battle for five cycles, refreshing only that stat's expiry and respecting the +/-6 cap. Record the comparison and chosen stat in the combat log. This deployment adaptation replaces the reference switch-in trigger because battles currently have no switching command. Ability reacquisition must not retrigger the entry bonus. The pure preview and enemy evaluator should show the same comparison without rolling RNG or modifying state.

Physical Dragon moves use Attack and Special Dragon moves use Special Attack; other types and Status moves receive no bonus. Determine the move's resolved type after conversions, so converted Dragon attacks qualify. Apply once per damage calculation, including each eligible area recipient, without stacking duplicate instances from the given and hidden slots. This continuous effect costs no AP, changes no stored stats or stages, and ends immediately when suppressed. Share its calculation with previews and enemy damage scoring.

Name: Dragonize
Description: The Pokémon's Normal-type moves become Dragon-type moves and their power is boosted by 20%.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Normal-type moves become Dragon-type moves and have their power multiplied by 1.2 (+20%). This effect comes after other effects that change a move's type, but before Ion Deluge and Electrify's effects.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Build a pre-ability move type from authored move/weather/item changes, then inspect active given and hidden slots in that order. Dragonize qualifies only when that pre-ability type is Normal; if it is the first eligible ability converter, replace the type with Dragon and give damaging moves one 1.2x base-power bonus. Only one ability conversion/bonus may apply per move, so a preceding eligible Normalize or other converter wins instead. Status moves change type without gaining damage. Apply the final profile consistently to STAB, effectiveness, absorption, targeting, previews, and AI without mutating the catalog or changing AP/range/shape. DEPENDENCY: implement this ordered resolved-move pipeline and reserve explicit final overrides for future Electrify/Ion Deluge rules.

Name: Drizzle
Description: The Pokémon makes it rain when it enters a battle.
Proposed: PROPOSED: On deployment, set the specified weather through the battle weather-state hook.
Exact Description: On entry, starts rain for 5 turns, or 8 turns if this Pokémon holds a Damp Rock. Rain multiplies Water-type damage by 1.5 (+50%) and Fire-type damage by 0.5 (-50%).
Game Implementation: on battle start summon rain for 5-8 cycles

Name: Drought
Description: Turns the sunlight harsh when the Pokémon enters a battle.
Proposed: PROPOSED: On deployment, set the specified weather through the battle weather-state hook.
Exact Description: On entry, starts harsh sunlight for 5 turns, or 8 turns if this Pokémon holds a Heat Rock. Sun multiplies Fire-type damage by 1.5 (+50%) and Water-type damage by 0.5 (-50%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: When the holder is initially deployed, replace ordinary weather with sun for five global cycles, expiring at battle time plus 50,000 AV. Sun uses the existing Fire damage x1.5, Water damage x0.5, and weather-sensitive speed hooks for every unit. A later ordinary weather setter replaces it; suppressors suspend weather effects while the saved timer keeps running. Resolve simultaneous deployment setters in stable battle-unit order and log the final winning weather. Do not reset the timer every holder turn or on simple ability reacquisition. Eight-cycle Heat Rock duration is gated on an authored compatible held-item modifier; default remains five. Recompute waiting AV after weather changes.

Name: Dry Skin
Description: Restores the Pokémon's HP in rain or when it is hit by Water-type moves. Reduces HP in harsh sunlight, and increases the damage received from Fire-type moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add an incoming-hit hook; check the described move or damage condition, then apply its prevention, healing, or stat response.
Exact Description: This Pokémon is immune to Water-type moves and restores 1/4 (25%) of its maximum HP, rounded down, when hit by a Water-type move. The power of Fire-type moves is multiplied by 1.25 (+25%) when used on this Pokémon. At the end of each turn, this Pokémon restores 1/8 (12.5%) of its maximum HP, rounded down, if the weather is Rain, and loses 1/8 (12.5%) of its maximum HP, rounded down, if the weather is Sun. The weather effects are prevented if this Pokémon is holding a Utility Umbrella.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Before incoming Water-move damage or secondary effects, absorb the hit and heal the holder by ceil(maximum HP/4), minimum 1 and capped at maximum HP, once per successful incoming move recipient. Incoming Fire damage uses a 1.25x base-power modifier. At each global cycle boundary, heal ceil(maximum HP/8) in rain or deal that amount of indirect damage in sun; other weather gives neither. These ceil rules intentionally match this game's HP rounding. Absorption and cycle effects are independent, never accumulate multipliers, and stop while suppressed. DEPENDENCY: extend absorption and incoming/cycle hooks; Utility Umbrella exceptions activate only after that item exists. Weather suppression disables weather effects while preserving Water absorption and Fire vulnerability.

Name: Early Bird
Description: The Pokémon awakens from sleep twice as fast as other Pokémon.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Shorten this unit sleep duration in the status-cycle update.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's sleep counter drops by 2 instead of 1.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: add a saved sleep status with a per-holder activation counter and clear action-blocking rules; sleep does not currently exist as a typed move effect. On each sleeping holder activation, decrement its remaining sleep count by 2 rather than 1, wake immediately at zero, and allow normal actions on that activation. A newly applied sleep counter is not reduced until the next activation. Reapplication refreshes to the new authored sleep count rather than stacking durations. This affects only the holder and has no probability, AP bonus, or general status immunity. Show both remaining sleep activations and Early Bird's accelerated decrement; switching-related resets remain outside this proposal.

Name: Earth Eater
Description: If hit by a Ground-type move, the Pokémon has its HP restored instead of taking damage.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add an incoming-hit hook; check the described move or damage condition, then apply its prevention, healing, or stat response.
Exact Description: This Pokémon is immune to Ground-type moves and restores 1/4 (25%) of its maximum HP, rounded down, when hit by a Ground-type move.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Extend the existing absorption family with Ground as the incoming type. After a successful hit check and resolved-type conversion, prevent all Ground move damage and attached on-hit effects against the holder, then heal ceil(maximum HP/4), minimum 1 and capped at maximum HP. Resolve once per holder per incoming move event, including area hits; misses do not heal, and overlapping absorption abilities must intercept only once using given-slot then hidden-slot order. This is immunity to Ground attacks, not flying movement or protection against lava, sandstorm, or arbitrary hazard zones. It costs no AP, persists while active, and needs matching pure damage, matchup, preview, AI, and ability-suppression support.

Name: Eelevate
Description: The Pokémon floats off the ground, making it immune to Ground-type moves, as well as the Spikes, Toxic Spikes, and Sticky Web statuses. When the Pokémon knocks out a target with an attack, its highest stat is boosted by 1 stage.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Check the described immunity or prevention rule before applying the affected status, move, stat, or field effect.
Exact Description: This Pokémon is immune to Ground-type attacks and the effects of Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Sticky Web, and the Arena Trap Ability. The effects of Gravity, Ingrain, Smack Down, Thousand Arrows, and Iron Ball nullify the immunity. Thousand Arrows can hit this Pokémon as if it did not have this Ability. This Pokémon's highest stat is raised by 1 stage if it attacks and knocks out another Pokémon. Stat stage changes are not considered. If multiple stats are tied, Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed are prioritized in that order.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Combine a Ground-attack immunity/airborne hazard profile with a KO reward. DEPENDENCY: distinguish attack grounding from traversal mobility and author Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Sticky Web, and grounding overrides before those interactions become playable; the current Stealth Rock zone still hits airborne units. After the holder directly KOs an opponent with its attack, raise its highest intrinsic non-HP, non-Movement stat by +1 for five cycles. Resolve ties Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, then Speed; ignore stages when selecting. Grant at most one boost per defeated target, refresh that stat's expiry, and reschedule Speed changes. Grounding removes only the immunity portion, while the KO bonus remains active.

Name: Effect Spore
Description: Contact with the Pokémon may inflict poison, sleep, or paralysis on the attacker.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After contact damage, run a post-hit reaction using the described chance, status, or ability-transfer effect.
Exact Description: A Pokémon making contact with this Pokémon has a 30% total chance to receive a status: 11% sleep, 10% paralysis, or 9% poison. Grass-type attackers and attackers protected by Overcoat or Safety Goggles are immune. Applicable status immunities still prevent the selected status. Gen 3: activation chance was 10% total.
Game Implementation: After contact damage, 30% chance to paralyze/sleep/poison the attacker(duration:paralyze-the entire game;sleep;2-5 turns;poison - entire game)

Name: Electric Surge
Description: Turns the ground into Electric Terrain when the Pokémon enters a battle.
Proposed: PROPOSED: On deployment, set Electric Terrain in a new battle-terrain state and apply its field effects.
Exact Description: On entry, starts Electric Terrain for 5 turns, or 8 turns if this Pokémon holds a Terrain Extender. Grounded Pokémon cannot fall asleep, and their Electric-type moves have 1.3x power (+30%). Gen 7: the power multiplier was 1.5x (+50%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: implement one saved battlefield-terrain enum with expiry, shared grounded checks, sleep-prevention hooks, damage previews, and AI support; terrain is distinct from map tiles and weather. At deployment, set Electric Terrain for five cycles (50,000 AV), replacing any earlier terrain. Grounded units on both sides cannot receive sleep, and their resolved Electric damaging moves receive 1.3x base power. Existing sleep is not cured. Grounded means the combat grounded profile, not merely standing on a plain tile. Terrain replacement or expiry removes the effects immediately; suppression prevents the setter from firing. Terrain Extender's eight-cycle variant remains gated on an actual item definition. Simultaneous setters resolve in stable battle-unit order.

Name: Electromorphosis
Description: The Pokémon becomes charged when it takes damage, boosting the power of the next Electric-type move the Pokémon uses.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: After this Pokémon is hit by a damaging move, it gains the charged effect. Its next Electric-type attack has double power (2x, a 100% increase). Using an Electric-type move other than Charge consumes the effect, even if it is a status move or misses. The effect otherwise persists until this Pokémon switches out. Repeated activation does not stack multipliers, and this Ability does not grant Charge's Special Defense stage increase.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After the holder loses HP to a direct damaging move, set a single saved charged flag. Repeated damaging hits refresh that same flag without increasing its strength. Its next declared Electric-type move consumes the flag, even on a miss or immunity; if damaging, that complete move event receives 2x base power against all its area recipients. Charge itself is excluded only when that move has an authored identifier. Indirect burn, weather, and tile damage do not charge the holder. The flag lasts until consumed or battle end, supplies no Special Defense stage, and grants no extra Attack command or AP. Preview consumption and powered damage without spending the flag or drawing RNG.

Name: Embody Aspect
Description: The Pokémon's heart fills with memories, causing the Mask to shine and one of the Pokémon's stats to be boosted.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described named stat modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: When Ogerpon Terastallizes, it gains the effect matching its mask: Teal Mask raises Speed by 1 stage, Wellspring Mask raises Special Defense by 1 stage, Hearthflame Mask raises Attack by 1 stage, and Cornerstone Mask raises Defense by 1 stage. The appropriate boost also activates when the Terastallized form switches back in. A +1 stage boost is normally 1.5x the unmodified stat when starting at stage 0.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: implement Ogerpon mask-form identifiers and an explicit Terastallization mechanic before using the reference trigger; Mega Evolution alone does not satisfy it. Once the holder enters its authored Terastallized mask form, grant exactly +1 to Speed for Teal, Special Defense for Wellspring, Attack for Hearthflame, or Defense for Cornerstone. The stage lasts five cycles, obeys +/-6, and refreshes only that stat's timer; Speed changes reschedule waiting AV. Save a once-per-battle activation flag because no switching command currently exists. Ordinary deployment, equipping an unregistered mask, or merely gaining this ability grants nothing. Restore ordinary form after battle and show the exact mask-to-stat mapping in the transformation preview.

Name: Emergency Exit
Description: The Pokémon, sensing danger, switches out when its HP becomes half or less.
Proposed: PROPOSED: At half HP or less, trigger a forced retreat if a legal reserve unit is available.
Exact Description: When this Pokémon has more than 1/2 (50%) its maximum HP and takes damage bringing it to 1/2 (50%) or less of its maximum HP, it immediately switches out to a chosen ally. This effect applies after all hits from a multi-hit move. This effect is prevented if the move had a secondary effect removed by the Sheer Force Ability. This effect applies to both direct and indirect damage, except Curse and Substitute on use, Belly Drum, Pain Split, and confusion damage.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: ADAPTATION: Once per battle, latch when actual HP damage crosses this holder from above 50% maximum HP to at/below 50%, before threshold Berry healing. Include residual damage, exclude deliberate HP costs, and suppress reactions removed by Sheer Force. After the complete triggering move/residual event, if alive, advance its next action by 2,500 AV, capped at current time, and grant +1 tile to its next ordinary Move. The bonus expires after that Move or at the end of its next usable turn. The Move still costs 1 AP and obeys normal legality/limits. Save the latch; no switching or forced displacement occurs. Match Wimp Out exactly.

Name: Fairy Aura
Description: Powers up each Pokémon’s Fairy-type moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: While this Pokémon is active, the power of Fairy-type moves used by active Pokémon is multiplied by 1.33.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While at least one living, unsuppressed Fairy Aura holder is deployed, multiply the base power of every resolved Fairy-type damaging move by 1.33 for both teams, including the holder. This battlefield-wide aura has no distance restriction, AP cost, stage duration, or deployment proc. Multiple Fairy Aura sources produce one modifier; a holder fainting removes its contribution immediately. Follow the existing custom Aura Break proposition: an active Aura Break replaces the bonus with 0.75x power rather than multiplying both. Calculate resolved type before checking eligibility, and apply the modifier once to each target's damage calculation. DEPENDENCY: add shared active-aura aggregation before publication.

Name: Filter
Description: Reduces the power of supereffective attacks that hit the Pokémon.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon receives 3/4 (75%) damage from supereffective attacks.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Immediately before final incoming attack damage, if the resolved type-effectiveness multiplier against the holder is greater than 1, multiply that damage by 0.75 using the shared fixed-point rounding. A 2x weakness therefore becomes effectively 1.5x; a 4x weakness becomes 3x before other independent modifiers. Neutral, resisted, immune, Status, and indirect damage are unaffected. Evaluate separately for each area recipient and each future authored hit, with no trigger charge, duration, or RNG. Duplicate copies of Filter never stack; other distinct defenses follow the published modifier order. Extend pure damage calculation, matchup information, enemy scoring, suppression, and combat feedback together so the preview agrees with actual HP loss.

Name: Fire Mane
Description: Boosts the power of the Pokémon's Fire-type moves by 50%.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's offensive stat is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%) while using a Fire-type attack.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: For every damaging move whose final resolved type is Fire, multiply the holder's relevant offensive stat by 1.5 before computing damage. Apply after its ordinary stat stages and applicable held-item modifiers; Physical moves use Attack and Special moves use Special Attack. This is a continuous ability modifier, not a +1 stage and not a weather setter, so it works in any weather and does not refresh stage timers. Normal STAB, sun/rain, and distinct abilities still apply in their shared order. Status Fire moves gain no numerical effect. Apply once per damage calculation, deduplicate identical ability IDs across both slots, and use the same result in previews, AI, and suppression handling.

Name: Flame Body
Description: Contact with the Pokémon may burn the attacker.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After contact damage, run a post-hit reaction using the described chance, status, or ability-transfer effect.
Exact Description: 30% chance a Pokémon making contact with this Pokémon will be burned.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After a successful contact-tagged damaging hit, use the defender's hit snapshot to roll one seeded 30% chance to burn the living attacker, even if this holder fainted from that hit. Apply Burn for two cycles (20,000 AV), refreshing only to a later expiry without stacking damage ticks; this temporary duration follows current status handling and needs designer review. Burn retains its physical-damage penalty and cycle tick. Misses, immunity, non-contact delivery, and damage-only chains cannot trigger the reaction; Long Reach removes contact eligibility. Apply status/immunity guards before consuming the reaction roll when possible. Previews show the chance and duration without RNG; feedback names the triggering ability, and KO settlement waits for the reaction.

Name: Flare Boost
Description: Powers up special moves when the Pokémon is burned.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: While this Pokémon is burned, the power of its special attacks is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While the holder's Burn timer is active, multiply the base power of its Special-category damaging moves by 1.5. Physical and Status moves receive no bonus, and Burn's existing periodic HP damage continues; this ability does not cure Burn or modify its timer. Evaluate the condition at move resolution so a cure before attacking removes the bonus immediately. Apply once to all eligible area damage calculations, with no extra AP, action, stage, or chance. Other distinct offensive modifiers combine through the common damage pipeline. DEPENDENCY: extend conditional ability evaluation to compare status expiry against battle time rather than merely checking for a stored status key, ensuring expired Burn cannot power the move.

Name: Flash Fire
Description: If hit by a Fire-type move, the Pokémon absorbs the flames and uses them to power up its own Fire-type moves.
Proposed: CURRENT RULES: Absorb Fire hits, set the charge status, and boost later Fire damage.
Exact Description: This Pokémon is immune to Fire-type moves. The first time it is hit by a Fire-type move, its offensive stat is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%) while using a Fire-type attack as long as it remains active and has this Ability. If this Pokémon is frozen, it cannot be defrosted by Fire-type attacks.
Game Implementation: absorbs fire damage and boosts fire moves by 50%(concurrent fire hits don’t boost it further)

Name: Flower Gift
Description: Boosts the Attack and Sp. Def stats of itself and allies in harsh sunlight.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Attack modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is a Cherrim and Sun is active, it changes to Sunshine Form and the Attack and Special Defense of it and its allies are multiplied by 1.5 (+50%). These effects are prevented if the Pokémon is holding a Utility Umbrella.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: add Cherrim's authored ordinary/Sunshine forms and a shared weather-aware ally-stat aura. During effective sun, a living Cherrim holder and every living teammate gain 1.5x effective Attack and Special Defense across the battlefield. This is a continuous modifier, not accumulating stages; multiple Flower Gift holders do not stack. Remove it immediately when sun ends, weather is suppressed, the source faints, or the ability is suppressed. Its visual Sunshine form follows the same condition and restores afterward without altering owned species. Utility Umbrella exceptions require the actual held-item rule before registration. Preserve Battery's separate custom Special-move bonus and ordinary AP rules. Previews must evaluate each recipient's actual affected defensive/offensive stat.

Name: Flower Veil
Description: Ally Grass-type Pokémon are protected from status conditions and the lowering of their stats.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described named stat modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: Grass-type Pokémon on this Pokémon's side cannot have their stat stages lowered by other Pokémon or have a non-volatile status condition inflicted on them by other Pokémon.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While a living unsuppressed holder is deployed, protect all living Grass-type teammates, including the holder when Grass-type, from major statuses and negative stat-stage deltas caused by another unit. Scope is battlefield-wide, consistent with the custom ally-support propositions; multiple sources do not stack. Existing statuses and negative stages remain until cured or expired, and self-inflicted drops or statuses still apply. Test the recipient's current battle types at effect time. Burn and paralysis guards can be implemented now; poison, sleep, and freeze require their typed status rules first. Route every effect through shared source-aware status/stage hooks so direct moves, abilities, and reflected effects respect this protection. Remove protection immediately when its last source disappears.

Name: Fluffy
Description: Halves the damage taken from moves that make direct contact, but doubles that of Fire-type moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After contact damage, run a post-hit reaction using the described chance, status, or ability-transfer effect.
Exact Description: This Pokémon receives 1/2 (50%) damage from contact moves, but double damage from Fire moves.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: For incoming damaging moves against the holder, apply 0.5x final damage when the resolved move makes contact, and independently apply 2x damage when its final type is Fire. A Fire contact move receives both modifiers and therefore returns to normal damage before other effects; a non-contact Fire move receives the full 2x vulnerability. Use the contact tag after Long Reach and equivalent contact overrides, rather than Physical category or melee delivery. No stage, RNG, charges, or periodic tick is involved. Effects persist while the ability is active and disappear on suppression. Weather, Burn, and tile hazards are unaffected. Share the two-factor modifier with pure damage previews and enemy scoring.

Name: Forecast
Description: The Pokémon transforms with the weather to change its type to Water, Fire, or Ice.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described type change in move or hit resolution and update the holder battle types for its stated duration.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is a Castform, its type changes to the current weather condition's type, except Sandstorm. This effect is prevented if this Pokémon is holding a Utility Umbrella and the weather is Rain or Sun.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: register Castform and its weather forms plus a reversible battle-type override. While the holder is Castform, effective sun makes it pure Fire, rain pure Water, and snow pure Ice; clear or sandstorm restores its original Normal type. Recalculate immediately after weather changes, expiry, suppression, or ability gain/loss, without changing HP, AP, stats, position, or owned species. Utility Umbrella suppression of sun/rain transformations requires the corresponding held-item definition. Repeated evaluation does not retrigger entry abilities or spend actions. Forecast changes combat typing and presentation only, so Flying traversal is not gained. Show the current form and resulting matchups in inspection, previews, and save restoration.

Name: Forewarn
Description: When it enters a battle, the Pokémon can tell one of the moves an opposing Pokémon has.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Run the described effect once on deployment, targeting the stated units or battle field.
Exact Description: On switch-in, this Pokémon is alerted to the move with the highest power, at random, known by an opposing Pokémon. This effect considers OHKO moves to have 150 power, Counter, Mirror Coat, and Metal Burst to have 120 power, every other attacking move with an unspecified power to have 80 power, and non-damaging moves to have 1 power.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: ADAPTATION FOR REVIEW: at deployment, identify the highest authored-power damaging move among all living opponents and mark its owner as Forewarn's threat for five cycles. Score future one-hit-KO moves as 150, authored retaliation moves as 120, and other variable-power damaging moves as 80; tie by stable opponent order, then equipped slot. Reveal the move name, AP cost, range, and shape in the log, and reduce direct damage from that marked move to this holder by 20% while marked. This defensive benefit makes the ability useful where inspection already exposes enemy moves. It triggers once per battle, consumes no RNG, and never changes the enemy loadout or the team's action economy.

Name: Friend Guard
Description: Reduces damage dealt to allies.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's allies receive 3/4 (75%) damage from other Pokémon's attacks.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While this living, unsuppressed holder is deployed, all its living teammates except itself receive 0.75x direct attack damage from either side. Scope is battlefield-wide, following the existing Battery support proposition; distance and formation do not restrict it. Multiple Friend Guard sources provide one 25% reduction to a given recipient, even if both ability slots or several units supply it. Burn, sandstorm, lava, recoil, and other indirect/self-damage remain unchanged. Apply after type effectiveness in the shared final-damage pipeline and remove immediately when no supporting source remains. No stage, duration counter, AP cost, or RNG is involved. UI previews and AI must account for the target's actual current allied sources.

Name: Frisk
Description: When it enters a battle, the Pokémon can check an opposing Pokémon's held item.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Run the described effect once on deployment, targeting the stated units or battle field.
Exact Description: On switch-in, this Pokémon identifies the held items of all opposing Pokémon.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: ADAPTATION FOR REVIEW: once at initial deployment, inspect all living opponents and record each held item in a persistent battle log panel. Because current inspection already exposes equipment, additionally mark the nearest opponent holding an active item for five cycles and reduce that opponent's item-derived offensive and defensive multipliers against this holder by 25% of their bonus portion; a 1.5x bonus becomes 1.375x. Break distance ties by stable battle-unit order; if none has an item, only reveal information. Do not disable consumables, Mega Stones, or Bag items. DEPENDENCY: item-modifier provenance and mark persistence must exist before the tactical bonus is registered; no repeated activation or item theft occurs.

Name: Full Metal Body
Description: Prevents other Pokémon’s moves or Abilities from lowering the Pokémon’s stats.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Check the described immunity or prevention rule before applying the affected status, move, stat, or field effect.
Exact Description: Prevents other Pokémon from lowering this Pokémon's stat stages.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Reject any negative delta to the holder's Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed stages when another unit caused it, whether through a move, ability, or item. Allow self-inflicted drops, positive stages, expiry to zero, direct effective-stat reductions, and global resets such as the custom Curious Medicine effect. Preserve the existing stage and expiry when a drop is blocked, and emit one Full Metal Body feedback event. No chance, AP cost, or limited trigger count applies. DEPENDENCY: shared stage events need source identity and a non-bypassable flag so ordinary Mold Breaker-style attacks cannot suppress this particular protection. It does not invent accuracy/evasion stages.

Name: Fur Coat
Description: Halves the damage from physical moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Defense is doubled (2x).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Continuously double the holder's effective Defense after applying its normal Defense stage and weather-dependent defensive modifiers, before a Physical move's damage denominator is calculated. This affects Physical damage through Defense rather than simply halving final damage, preserving the formula's rounding behavior. Special attacks, indirect damage, maximum HP, and stored intrinsic/rank stats remain unchanged. Apply one 2x modifier regardless of duplicate ability IDs; distinct Defense modifiers combine in a documented order. The bonus has no duration, deployment trigger, or AP cost and disappears immediately when the ability is suppressed. Extend the pure damage calculation and enemy scoring, then expose the effective defensive multiplier in inspection and damage previews.

Name: Gale Wings
Description: Gives priority to the Pokémon's Flying-type moves while its HP is full.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Speed or action-order rule in the battle scheduler, checking its stated condition.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is at full HP, its Flying-type moves have their priority increased by 1. Gen 6: the +1 priority applied at any HP.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: ADAPTATION FOR REVIEW: since the AV engine has no move-priority queue, a Flying-type damaging move declared while the holder is at full HP advances only the holder's next scheduled action by 2,500 AV. Apply the advance once per completed Attack command, including an area move, even if it later misses; do not create an immediate extra turn or reset the current Attack/Move flags. Clamp the resulting next action at the current battle time. Losing full HP before declaration prevents the effect; healing back to full restores eligibility. The ordinary 3 AP gain, banking, and 650,000/effective-Speed interval remain intact. Preview the exact next-action change without RNG.

Name: Galvanize
Description: Normal-type moves become Electric-type moves. The power of those moves is boosted a little.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Normal-type moves become Electric-type moves and have their power multiplied by 1.2 (+20%). This effect comes after other effects that change a move's type, but before Ion Deluge and Electrify's effects.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Derive the move's pre-ability type from authored move/weather/item changes, then inspect given before unlocked hidden ability. Galvanize qualifies only when that pre-ability type is Normal; if it is the first eligible converter, replace the type with Electric and add one 1.2x base-power bonus to damaging moves. A preceding eligible converter wins, and no second ability conversion or bonus stacks. Status moves change type without gaining damage. Use the final profile for STAB, immunity, absorption/redirection, terrain, targeting, previews, and AI while preserving AP, range, area, category, delivery, and tags. DEPENDENCY: add ordered resolved-move hooks, with separately authored future final overrides, rather than mutating catalog records.

Name: Gluttony
Description: If the Pokémon is holding a Berry to be eaten when its HP is low, it will instead eat the Berry when its HP drops to half or less.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a held-item trigger that checks the described condition and applies the stated item interaction.
Exact Description: When this Pokémon is holding a Berry that usually activates with 1/4 (25%) or less of its maximum HP, it is eaten at 1/2 (50%) or less of its maximum HP instead.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: When an eligible held Berry has an authored low-HP automatic trigger normally requiring HP at or below 25%, check it instead at or below 50% maximum HP. Evaluate immediately after damage and after equipping or acquiring an eligible Berry in battle, resolving consumption only once before subsequent reactions. Preserve that Berry's actual heal, cure, or stage effect, and let Cheek Pouch/Cud Chew receive the resulting single consumption event. Berries without the quarter-HP trigger are unchanged. DEPENDENCY: add typed Berry metadata, automatic-consumption ordering, and used-item history; current generic held-item actions cannot imply these rules. The ability adds no Berry, chance, AP, or healing of its own, and empty-handed holders gain nothing.

Name: Good as Gold
Description: A body of pure, solid gold gives the Pokémon full immunity to other Pokémon's status moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described named stat modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: This Pokémon is immune to Status moves.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While active, prevent Status-category moves used by another unit from applying their targeted effects to this holder, including hostile stage changes, status, forced displacement, and targeted recovery. It does not block damaging moves' secondary effects, ability/item effects, or indirect damage. Self-used Status moves remain legal. Global weather, Trick Room, and future terrain setters still create their battlefield state; immunity concerns a recipient effect, not deletion of the whole cast. Apply rejection separately to this recipient in an area move so other units resolve normally. DEPENDENCY: tag target-directed versus field effects in shared resolution. No RNG, AP refund, duration, or trigger limit applies; show rejected effects in previews and logs.

Name: Gooey
Description: Contact with the Pokémon lowers the attacker's Speed stat.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After contact damage, run a post-hit reaction using the described chance, status, or ability-transfer effect.
Exact Description: Pokémon making contact with this Pokémon have their Speed lowered by 1 stage.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After a successful contact-tagged damaging hit, use the defender's hit snapshot to lower the living attacker's Speed by 1 stage for five cycles, even if this holder fainted. Trigger with 100% probability once per primary hit event; misses, immunity, damage-only chains, and Long Reach do not qualify. Each valid later trigger adds another -1 down to -6 and refreshes the attacker's Speed-stage expiry, including at the cap. Respect Clear Body, Flower Veil, Mirror Armor, Contrary, and shared stage rules rather than writing the stat directly. Rescale a waiting attacker's remaining AV immediately; if currently acting, the change affects its next interval. No AP is stolen and no turn is skipped.

Name: Gorilla Tactics
Description: Boosts the Pokémon’s Attack stat but only allows the use of the first selected move.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Attack modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Attack is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%), but it can only select the first move it executes. These effects are prevented while this Pokémon is Dynamaxed.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While active, multiply the holder's effective Attack by 1.5. After it successfully declares its first legal equipped Attack move, save that move ID as the lock for the rest of battle; subsequent Attack commands may select only that move, while Move, Special, Pass, and banked AP remain available. A miss still commits the lock because the move was executed; rejected commands do not. Ability suppression temporarily removes both multiplier and restriction without deleting the saved lock, and reacquisition restores it. DEPENDENCY: add a saved move-lock field and shared legality/AI/UI filtering. There is no Dynamax system, so do not invent an exemption. Restore ordinary choices after battle.

Name: Grass Pelt
Description: Boosts the Pokémon's Defense stat on Grassy Terrain.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Defense modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: If Grassy Terrain is active, this Pokémon's Defense is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: During active Grassy Terrain, multiply this holder's effective Defense by 1.5 before Physical damage calculation. This is a continuous condition, independent of whether the holder is grounded; it adds no Defense stage and has no separate five-cycle timer. Terrain expiry/replacement or ability suppression removes the modifier immediately, and repeated terrain updates do not accumulate bonuses. Special attacks and indirect damage remain unchanged. DEPENDENCY: create a saved battlefield-terrain type and expiry shared with Grassy Surge; existing grass scenery, moss tiles, mud, and Stealth Rock zones do not count as Grassy Terrain. Apply once per calculation and use the same effective Defense in previews, inspection, and enemy scoring.

Name: Grassy Surge
Description: Turns the ground into Grassy Terrain when the Pokémon enters a battle.
Proposed: PROPOSED: On deployment, set Grassy Terrain in a new battle-terrain state and apply its field effects.
Exact Description: On entry, starts Grassy Terrain for 5 turns, or 8 turns if this Pokémon holds a Terrain Extender. Grounded Pokémon recover 1/16 (6.25%) of their maximum HP each turn, and their Grass-type moves have 1.3x power (+30%). Earthquake, Bulldoze, and Magnitude deal half damage to grounded targets. Gen 7: the Grass power multiplier was 1.5x (+50%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: add saved battlefield terrain, grounded-recipient checks, per-cycle terrain processing, and move identifiers for the listed seismic exceptions. At deployment, set Grassy Terrain for five cycles, replacing earlier terrain. Grounded units on both teams heal ceil(maximum HP/16), minimum 1 and capped, at each global cycle boundary, and their resolved Grass damaging moves receive 1.3x base power. Earthquake, Bulldoze, and Magnitude deal half damage to grounded recipients; other Ground moves are unchanged. Terrain removal ends all effects immediately. Eight-cycle Terrain Extender duration requires a real item rule. Simultaneous setters follow stable battle-unit order; no recurring reapplication occurs on the holder's turns, and map grass itself does not activate the terrain.

Name: Grim Neigh
Description: When the Pokémon knocks out a target, it utters a terrifying neigh, which boosts its Sp. Atk stat.
Proposed: PROPOSED: At the described trigger, raise the holder named stat through battle stat stages or an effective-stat modifier.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Special Attack is raised by 1 stage if it attacks and knocks out another Pokémon.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After this holder's direct damaging move reduces a living opponent to 0 HP, grant the surviving holder +1 Special Attack for five cycles. Each distinct opponent KO can trigger once, including several opponents from one area move; process recipients in stable battle-unit order and refresh that stat's expiry after every accepted stage gain, up to +6. Damage-only chains attributable to the holder count as its attack damage, while weather, hazards, burn ticks, allied KOs, and ability retaliation do not. No bonus applies after the holder itself has fainted. Respect shared stage interception and suppression, grant no AP or extra Attack command, and show anticipated KO rewards without committing them in preview.

Name: Guard Dog
Description: Boosts the Pokémon’s Attack stat if intimidated. Moves and items that would force the Pokémon to switch out also fail to work.
Proposed: PROPOSED: At the described trigger, raise the holder Attack through battle stat stages or an effective-stat modifier.
Exact Description: This Pokémon is immune to the effect of the Intimidate Ability and raises its Attack by 1 stage instead. This Pokémon cannot be forced to switch out by another Pokémon's attack or item.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: When an Intimidate source attempts its custom Attack -1 aura entry effect on this holder, cancel that drop and grant the holder +1 Attack for five cycles instead. Record source/recipient inside-aura transitions so leaving and reentering can retrigger once per real crossing, matching the existing Intimidate proposition without repeated stationary procs. Standard +/-6 caps and expiry refresh apply. ADAPTATION FOR REVIEW: also reject hostile push/pull displacement against the holder, replacing the otherwise inactive forced-switch immunity in a game without switching. Voluntary Move actions and tile-entry hazards remain normal. DEPENDENCY: pass originating ability and displacement source through shared effect guards so unrelated Attack drops are not converted.

Name: Gulp Missile
Description: When the Pokémon uses Surf or Dive, it will come back with prey. When it takes damage, it will spit out the prey to attack.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is a Cramorant, it changes forme when it hits a target with Surf or uses the first turn of Dive successfully. It becomes Gulping Form with an Arrokuda in its mouth if it has more than 1/2 (50%) of its maximum HP remaining, or Gorging Form with a Pikachu in its mouth if it has 1/2 (50%) or less of its maximum HP remaining. If Cramorant gets hit in Gulping or Gorging Form, it spits the Arrokuda or Pikachu at its attacker, even if it has no HP remaining. The projectile deals damage equal to 1/4 (25%) of the target's maximum HP, rounded down; this damage is blocked by the Magic Guard Ability but not by a substitute. An Arrokuda also lowers the target's Defense by 1 stage, and a Pikachu paralyzes the target. Cramorant will return to normal if it spits out a projectile, switches out, or Dynamaxes.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: register compatible Cramorant forms, Surf/Dive identifiers, stored projectile state, and post-hit retaliation that can resolve after holder KO. A committed Surf execution or successful first Dive phase arms one projectile: Arrokuda above half HP, Pikachu otherwise; repeated qualifying moves replace rather than stack it. The next successful direct damaging hit consumes it and deals ceil(attacker maximum HP/4), minimum 1, as indirect ability damage, even if Cramorant faints. Arrokuda adds Defense -1 for five cycles; Pikachu adds paralysis for two cycles. Misses and hazards do not release it. Magic Guard can block retaliation damage. Return to ordinary form after release/battle end, preserve ordinary action limits, and show armed state in inspection.

Name: Guts
Description: It's so gutsy that having a status condition boosts the Pokémon's Attack stat.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Attack modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon has a non-volatile status condition, its Attack is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%). This Pokémon's physical attacks ignore the burn effect of halving damage.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: While the holder has an active major status, multiply its effective Attack by 1.5 before Physical damage calculation, and ignore Burn's usual 0.5x physical-damage penalty. Burn's periodic HP loss and paralysis's Speed penalty still occur; this ability does not cure, extend, or inflict a status. Count active Burn and paralysis using their expiry timestamps; future poison, sleep, and freeze qualify only after their own typed systems exist. Volatile debuffs such as move lock or confusion do not count. The bonus is continuous, never stacks per status, and ends immediately upon cure, expiry, or suppression. Share the resulting Attack and Burn exception with pure previews and enemy scoring.

Name: Hadron Engine
Description: Turns the ground into Electric Terrain when the Pokémon enters a battle. The futuristic engine within the Pokémon also boosts its Sp. Atk stat on Electric Terrain.
Proposed: PROPOSED: At the described trigger, raise the holder named stat through battle stat stages or an effective-stat modifier.
Exact Description: On entry, starts Electric Terrain for 5 turns, or 8 turns with a Terrain Extender. While Electric Terrain is active, this Pokémon's Special Attack is multiplied by approximately 4/3 (about +33.33%), even if it is not grounded. The terrain also gives grounded Pokémon's Electric moves 1.3x power and prevents them from falling asleep.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: implement Electric Terrain's saved state, expiry, grounded checks, sleep guard, and shared damage support before registering this ability. At initial deployment, create Electric Terrain for five cycles, replacing earlier terrain. During that terrain, multiply the holder's effective Special Attack by 4/3 even while airborne. Grounded units on both teams additionally receive terrain's 1.3x Electric base power and prevention of new sleep. Multiple terrain setters do not stack the field; other Hadron holders do not multiply this holder's personal bonus repeatedly. Terrain expiry or suppression removes the applicable bonus immediately. Eight-cycle extension requires an authored Terrain Extender. Log the setter once and reschedule only effects that actually change Speed.

Name: Harvest
Description: May create another Berry after one is used.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After this unit consumes a Berry, use the described chance to return that Berry to its held-item slot.
Exact Description: If the last item this Pokémon used is a Berry, there is a 50% chance it gets restored at the end of each turn. If Sun is active, this chance is 100%.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: add typed Berry consumption events, saved last-consumed-Berry identity, and item restoration ownership before enabling Harvest. At each global cycle boundary, if the holder is alive, empty-handed, and its most recent eligible consumed item was a Berry not already restored from that consumption, make one seeded 50% restoration roll; use 100% during effective sun. Success returns that Berry to its held slot and consumes the restoration claim, preventing the same event from creating duplicate items. A later genuine consumption creates a new eligible claim. Failure leaves the claim for the next cycle. Non-Berry consumables and Bag items are ineligible. Recovered Berry use can trigger its normal interactions; no extra AP or forced consumption is granted.

Name: Healer
Description: Sometimes cures the status conditions of the Pokémon's allies.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described named stat modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: 30% chance this Pokémon's ally has its non-volatile status condition cured at the end of each turn.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: At each global cycle boundary, choose one living allied unit other than the holder within 2 Manhattan tiles that has at least one active major status. Prefer the lowest HP fraction, then shortest distance, then stable battle-unit order. Roll one seeded 30% chance; on success clear one status in the fixed order sleep, freeze, poison, Burn, paralysis. Only currently implemented statuses participate, with future types gated on their own rules. This local tactical adaptation needs designer review because the reference has one active ally rather than a full squad. It never cures the holder, stages, move locks, or confusion; no eligible ally means no roll. Show the chosen recipient and chance without consuming preview RNG.

Name: Heatproof
Description: The Pokémon's heatproof body halves the damage taken from Fire-type moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: If a Pokémon uses a Fire-type attack against this Pokémon, that Pokémon's offensive stat is halved (0.5x) when calculating the damage to this Pokémon. This Pokémon takes half of the usual burn damage, rounded down.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: When another unit's resolved Fire-type damaging move hits the holder, multiply that move's selected offensive stat by 0.5 for this recipient before calculating damage. Apply to both Physical and Special Fire attacks, regardless of contact or weather; other types remain normal. At each Burn tick, halve the otherwise computed HP loss and round using the game's ceil/minimum-1 policy, an intentional tactical rounding adaptation. Heatproof does not prevent or cure Burn, reduce lava/sandstorm, or grant Fire absorption. The modifiers are continuous and nonstacking for duplicate IDs. Share recipient-specific offensive-stat handling with pure damage previews and enemy scoring, and disable the benefit immediately while the ability is suppressed.

Name: Heavy Metal
Description: Doubles the Pokémon's weight.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Store the weight modifier on the unit and read it in weight-sensitive move effects.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's weight is doubled (2x). This effect is calculated after the effect of Autotomize, and before the effect of Float Stone.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: add species mass in kilograms, a shared effective-mass resolver, weight-based move formulas, and any weight-driven legality checks before publishing Heavy Metal. While the ability is active, double this holder's effective mass after authored Autotomize reductions and before Float Stone's item modifier; do not change HP, Defense, Speed, Movement, AP, or traversal flags. The result is continuous rather than a stage or stacking deployment bonus, so suppression immediately restores ordinary mass without altering stored species data. Preview weight-dependent power separately for each target and use the same result for AI. Current moves have no mass calculation, so this proposal remains explicitly gated rather than inventing an unsupported passive Defense bonus.

Name: Honey Gather
Description: The Pokémon may gather Honey after a battle.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Resolve in the route reward phase; grant the described item or benefit and record it in run inventory.
Exact Description: After a battle, if this Pokémon holds no item, it may obtain Honey. The chance is 5% at levels 1-10, 10% at 11-20, 15% at 21-30, 20% at 31-40, 25% at 41-50, 30% at 51-60, 35% at 61-70, 40% at 71-80, 45% at 81-90, and 50% at 91-100. Has no in-battle effect.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: register Honey as a real reward item with a concrete use, acquisition cap, and Bag representation before enabling this ability. After battle settlement, once per deployed surviving empty-handed holder, roll the run's seeded reward RNG using chance min(50%, 5% times ceil(level/10)); levels 1-10 receive 5%, 11-20 receive 10%, through 91-100 at 50%. On success add exactly one Honey to the Bag and record the settled battle/holder ID so reload cannot reroll or duplicate it. Fainted holders and reserves receive no roll, an explicit participation adaptation. Honey Gather has no in-battle effect, consumes no combat RNG, and never overwrites an existing held item.

Name: Hospitality
Description: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it showers its ally with hospitality, restoring a small amount of the ally's HP
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described field or aura effect to the stated allies or opponents while the holder is deployed.
Exact Description: On switch-in, this Pokémon restores 1/4 (25%) of its ally's maximum HP, rounded down.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: At initial deployment, heal one living allied unit other than the holder within 3 Manhattan tiles by ceil(that ally's maximum HP/4), minimum 1 and capped at maximum HP. Choose the ally missing the greatest HP fraction, then the closest tile, then stable battle-unit order. This single-recipient tactical adaptation avoids multiplying the reference's one-ally heal across a six-unit squad and needs designer review. Resolve after deployment occupancy is established and before first turns; no injured eligible ally means no effect. Trigger once per battle, with no AP cost, reserve heal, revival, or retrigger from ability reacquisition. Record the chosen recipient and amount in feedback; healing remains subject to shared heal-block rules when implemented.

Name: Huge Power
Description: Doubles the Pokémon's Attack stat.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Attack modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Attack is doubled (2x).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Multiply the holder's effective Attack by 2 after ordinary Attack stages and relevant held-item modifiers, before Physical damage calculation. Huge Power and Pure Power share one nonstacking family: any combination across both active slots provides 2x total, never 4x. This continuous modifier does not alter stored species/rank stats, create stages, or expire with them; critical hits retain it. Special and Status moves gain nothing, while AP gain, Movement, Speed, and attack frequency remain unchanged. Suppression removes the family multiplier only when no active source remains. Other distinct modifiers such as Guts follow the shared order. Use the same effective Attack in inspection, pure damage previews, enemy scoring, and resolution without RNG.

Name: Hunger Switch
Description: The Pokémon changes its form, alternating between its Full Belly Mode and Hangry Mode after the end of every turn.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Run the described passive effect at each battle cycle tick while the holder is active.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is a Morpeko, it changes formes between its Full Belly Mode and Hangry Mode at the end of each turn.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: register Morpeko's Full Belly/Hangry forms, Aura Wheel's form-dependent type rule, reversible battle forms, and saved toggle state. Start a fresh battle in Full Belly Mode; after each completed holder turn, including Pass, toggle exactly once to the other mode. Form changes do not grant AP, refresh Attack/Move availability, retrigger entry abilities, or reset status/stage timers. The resolved form controls only the authored type/move/stat differences; never infer missing form data from its name. Suppression freezes the toggle and normalizes the presentation to the authored ordinary form, with state behavior documented on restoration. The owned Pokémon returns to Full Belly after battle, and the next mode is visible before ending its turn.

Name: Hustle
Description: Boosts the Pokémon's Attack stat but lowers its accuracy.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described accuracy or evasion change in attack hit-chance resolution under its stated condition.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Attack is multiplied by 1.5 (+50%) and the accuracy of its physical attacks is multiplied by 0.8 (-20%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Continuously multiply the holder's effective Attack by 1.5 for Physical damage calculation, while multiplying the hit chance of its Physical-category damaging moves by 0.8. Base moves currently hit at 100%, so an otherwise ordinary Physical attack becomes 80%; target evasion factors combine multiplicatively and cap within 0-100%. Special and Status moves retain normal hit chance and gain no power. Roll once per eligible target using combat RNG after legality checks; a miss applies no damage or on-hit effects. No Guard overrides the hit penalty. The ability changes no stage, duration, AP cost, range, or number of attacks, and previews must display the adjusted chance without rolling.

Name: Hydration
Description: Cures the Pokémon's status conditions in rain.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described named stat modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: This Pokémon has its non-volatile status condition cured at the end of each turn if Rain is active. This effect is prevented if this Pokémon is holding a Utility Umbrella.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: At each global cycle boundary during effective rain, clear all active major statuses from the living holder before its ordinary residual status-damage pass. Burn and paralysis can participate now; poison, sleep, and freeze require authored status systems before registration with them. Existing negative stages, confusion, move locks, and HP loss are unaffected. There is no activation chance, AP cost, or separate duration; reapplication during rain can be cured again at the next boundary. If rain ends, is suppressed, or this ability is suppressed before the boundary, no cure occurs. Utility Umbrella's exception remains gated on its held-item definition. Clearing paralysis must immediately rescale the holder's waiting AV through the shared Speed scheduler.

Name: Hyper Cutter
Description: The Pokémon's prized, mighty pincers prevent other Pokémon from lowering its Attack stat.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Attack modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: Prevents other Pokémon from lowering this Pokémon's Attack stat stage.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Prevent any negative Attack-stage delta caused by another unit's move, ability, or held item from affecting the holder. Block the drop before Contrary, Mirror Armor, and reactive stat-loss checks according to the shared prevention order; a prevented drop does not count as a stat loss. Positive Attack changes, self-inflicted drops, ordinary stage expiry, and global stat resets remain allowed. This does not prevent direct continuous Attack multipliers, Burn's damage penalty, or changes to other stats. There is no chance, duration, AP cost, or limited trigger count. DEPENDENCY: source-aware shared stage events must cover all effect families so the immunity is consistent in engine resolution, preview, AI, suppression, and feedback.

Name: Ice Body
Description: The Pokémon gradually regains HP in snow.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described field or aura effect to the stated allies or opponents while the holder is deployed.
Exact Description: If Snow is active, this Pokémon restores 1/16 (6.25%) of its maximum HP, rounded down, at the end of each turn. Gen 8 and earlier: activates in hail instead of snow and also prevents hail damage.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: At every global cycle boundary while snow is the effective weather, heal the living holder by ceil(maximum HP/16), minimum 1 and capped at maximum HP. This ceil rounding intentionally matches current periodic healing. No HP is restored in other weather, while weather suppression or ability suppression disables that boundary's effect without pausing the saved weather timer. The ability provides no additional Ice-type physical-defense multiplier; ordinary snow already grants the existing benefit to Ice types. Do not add a separate hail weather kind or claim immunity to sandstorm, Burn, lava, or hazards. Repeated cycles can heal again; multiple copies of Ice Body on one holder produce one tick. Preview the amount and next boundary.

Name: Ice Face
Description: The Pokémon's ice head can take a physical attack as a substitute, but the attack also changes the Pokémon's appearance. The ice will be restored when it snows.
Proposed: PROPOSED: At the described trigger, modify the holder Attack through battle stat stages or an effective-stat modifier.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is an Eiscue, the first physical hit it takes in battle deals 0 neutral damage. Its ice face is then broken and it changes forme to Noice Face. Eiscue regains its Ice Face forme when Snow begins or when Eiscue switches in while Snow is active. Confusion damage also breaks the ice face. Gen 8: hail restores Ice Face instead of snow.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: register Eiscue's Ice Face/Noice forms and a saved shield state. Before the first successful direct Physical damaging hit, prevent its HP damage, spend the shield, and transform to Noice Face; Special attacks and indirect damage bypass the shield without spending it. An effective weather transition into snow restores the shield and Ice Face once for that transition, including initial snowy deployment; continuously remaining in snow does not rebuild it each cycle. Repeated same-weather setters count only if they genuinely end and restart the snow instance, a designer-review choice. Apply authored form stats with rank preserved and proportional AV rescheduling; ordinary secondary effects still resolve. Restore ordinary species after battle; confusion interactions require its missing status system.

Name: Ice Scales
Description: The Pokémon is protected by ice scales, which halve the damage taken from special moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon receives 1/2 (50%) damage from special attacks.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Multiply final direct damage received by the holder from Special-category moves by 0.5, after ordinary type and weather modifiers. Physical attacks and indirect damage from Burn, sandstorm, lava, hazards, recoil, or abilities remain unchanged; a move's ranged delivery or projectile tag does not make it Special. Check the resolved move category independently for every recipient and future authored hit. The modifier has no chance, stage, AP cost, duration, or trigger charge and disappears immediately when the ability is suppressed. Duplicate ability IDs do not stack. Use the shared final-damage modifier and fixed-point rounding so battle resolution, pure previews, enemy scoring, and displayed damage estimates all agree.

Name: Illuminate
Description: By illuminating its surroundings, the Pokémon prevents its accuracy from being lowered.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described accuracy or evasion change in attack hit-chance resolution under its stated condition.
Exact Description: Prevents other Pokémon from lowering this Pokémon's accuracy stat stage. This Pokémon ignores a target's evasiveness stat stage. Gen 8 and earlier: no battle effect; when leading the party, doubled (2x) the rate of ordinary wild encounters in games with that overworld mechanic.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: ADAPTATION FOR REVIEW: because the game has no accuracy/evasion stages, the holder's damaging moves ignore ability-derived evasion penalties such as Sand Veil and Snow Cloak, while still checking range, line of sight, type immunity, protection, and absorption. Do not remove the holder's own Hustle penalty or any authored move accuracy. A future accuracy-stage system should additionally reject opponent-caused accuracy drops and ignore target evasion stages, using the same shared hit context. This continuous self-only benefit consumes no RNG beyond the ordinary final hit roll and changes no AP, range, or stages. The former overworld encounter-rate function is inapplicable to the fixed route graph and is intentionally omitted.

Name: Illusion
Description: The Pokémon fools opponents by entering battle disguised as the last Pokémon in its Trainer's party.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described field or aura effect to the stated allies or opponents while the holder is deployed.
Exact Description: When this Pokémon switches in, it appears as the last unfainted Pokémon in its party until it takes direct damage from another Pokémon's attack. This Pokémon's actual level and HP are displayed instead of those of the mimicked Pokémon.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: add presentation-only disguise metadata and an explicit enemy-planner information policy. At deployment, choose the last living owned party member other than the holder by saved roster order; if unavailable, use the last living teammate by stable battle order. Display that species/name sprite while retaining the holder's actual HP, level, types, moves, stats, and collision. The first successful direct damaging hit breaks the disguise for the rest of battle; indirect damage, misses, and zero-damage immunity do not. No action, AP, or stat change is granted. To make the illusion meaningful, AI may initially evaluate visible typing until the disguise breaks, but player previews must clearly expose uncertainty; this tactical information adaptation needs designer review.

Name: Immunity
Description: The Pokémon's immune system prevents it from being poisoned.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Reject poison when a status effect is applied to this unit.
Exact Description: This Pokémon cannot be poisoned. Gaining this Ability while poisoned cures it.
Game Implementation: immune to poison

Name: Imposter
Description: The Pokémon transforms itself into the Pokémon it's facing.
Proposed: PROPOSED: On deployment, copy the facing target permitted battle stats, types, and moves for this battle.
Exact Description: On switch-in, this Pokémon Transforms into the opposing Pokémon that is facing it. If there is no Pokémon at that position, this Pokémon does not Transform.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: DEPENDENCY: implement temporary copied profiles, copyable-ability metadata, transform-safe moves/forms, and saved restoration. Once at deployment, select the nearest living opponent within 5 Manhattan tiles, tied by stable battle-unit order. Copy its current types, mobility permissions, five non-HP combat stats, move slots, and stage values with their exact expiry timestamps, retaining holder HP/maximum HP, level, rank identity, item, AP, position, and action flags. Copied intrinsic values already include target rank; never multiply them again. Replace only the effective slot supplying Imposter with the target's effective given ability; preserve the other slot and reject uncopyable/duplicate combinations. This spatial adaptation replaces facing-based entry logic. No owned profile changes; restore battle originals afterward and reschedule Speed proportionally.

Name: Infiltrator
Description: The Pokémon's moves are unaffected by the target's barriers, substitutes, and the like.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Let this unit attacks bypass barrier and substitute-style protection effects.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's moves ignore substitutes and the opposing side's Reflect, Light Screen, Safeguard, Mist, and Aurora Veil.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Let the holder's moves ignore target-side temporary protection effects explicitly tagged substitute, Reflect, Light Screen, Safeguard, Mist, or Aurora Veil. Damaging moves bypass only the appropriate screen/substitute factor; targeted status and stage effects bypass only Safeguard/Mist, while ordinary immunity, ability defenses, hit chance, cover, range, walls, and line of sight still apply. This is continuous and self-only, with no AP surcharge, stage duration, RNG, or extra attack. DEPENDENCY: none of those side-screen/substitute systems currently has a typed implementation, so add their tags, HP pools where needed, previews, and effect guards first. Do not silently treat map cover or all defensive abilities as equivalent to those absent systems.

Name: Innards Out
Description: Damages the attacker landing the finishing hit by the amount equal to its last HP.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add an incoming-hit hook; check the described move or damage condition, then apply its prevention, healing, or stat response.
Exact Description: If this Pokémon is knocked out with a move, that move's user loses HP equal to the amount of damage inflicted on this Pokémon.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: When another unit's direct damaging move KOs this holder, after that hit record the holder's actual HP removed, excluding overkill, and deal the same amount to the move's source as indirect ability damage. Resolve once for the lethal hit; later area recipients do not retrigger it, and an already fainted attacker cannot lose additional HP. Weather, Burn, tile hazards, recoil, self-damage, and ability retaliation do not trigger Innards Out. Magic Guard and shared indirect-damage immunity can prevent the retaliation; it cannot recursively trigger itself. DEPENDENCY: add an on-KO hook before result settlement and preserve both simultaneous defeats until the battle-result rule resolves. Log the recorded amount rather than recomputing damage.

Name: Inner Focus
Description: The Pokémon's intense focus prevents it from flinching or being affected by Intimidate.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After the described attack connects, run a chance-based flinch reaction in the post-hit hook.
Exact Description: This Pokémon cannot be made to flinch. This Pokémon is immune to the effect of the Intimidate Ability.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Reject flinch and any Attack-stage drop originating specifically from the custom Intimidate aura against this holder. Ordinary negative Attack stages from other sources still apply, and the ability does not prevent paralysis, action-delay moves, or reduced Speed. DEPENDENCY: add a saved flinch/skip-next-activation state and source-aware stage guards before publishing the flinch portion. A blocked flinch never consumes the holder's turn or AP; a blocked Intimidate entry does not count as a real stat loss for Defiant/Competitive. This protection is continuous, self-only, deterministic, and unlimited while unsuppressed. Respect the custom Intimidate five-Manhattan-tile enter/reenter tracking without granting a retaliatory stage or immunity to unrelated push/pull effects.

Name: Insomnia
Description: The Pokémon's insomnia prevents it from falling asleep.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Reject sleep when a status effect is applied to this unit.
Exact Description: This Pokémon cannot fall asleep. Gaining this Ability while asleep cures it.
Game Implementation: immune to sleep

Name: Intimidate
Description: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it intimidates opposing Pokémon and makes them cower, lowering their Attack stats.
Proposed: PROPOSED: On deployment, lower the Attack stage of opposing units through the battle stat-stage hook.
Exact Description: On switch-in, this Pokémon lowers the Attack of opposing Pokémon by 1 stage. Pokémon with the Inner Focus, Oblivious, Own Tempo, or Scrappy Abilities and Pokémon behind a substitute are immune.
Game Implementation: Aura: Units within 5 tiles have their attack lowered by -1 (going in and out will retrigger it)

Name: Intrepid Sword
Description: Boosts the Pokémon’s Attack stat the first time the Pokémon enters a battle.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Apply the described Attack modifier in battle stat calculation while its condition is active.
Exact Description: On switch-in, this Pokémon's Attack is raised by 1 stage. Once per battle. Gen 8: the +1 Attack boost activated on every entry, rather than once per battle.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After deployment occupancy and initial continuous modifiers are established, raise this holder's Attack by 1 stage for five cycles. Resolve once per battle and save the spent flag even if the stage was blocked, capped, subsequently reset, or expired; ability suppression at deployment delays no automatic catch-up unless explicitly authored later. This replaces the reference switch-in with the game's actual deployment event. The stage respects +/-6 and uses the ordinary shared stage mechanism, so it can be copied, reversed, or cleared by supported effects. It costs no AP and changes no action count. Simple ability reacquisition, Mega re-evaluation, healing, or battle reload must not repeat the bonus.

Name: Iron Barbs
Description: Inflicts damage on the attacker upon contact with iron barbs.
Proposed: PROPOSED: After contact damage, run a post-hit reaction using the described chance, status, or ability-transfer effect.
Exact Description: Pokémon making contact with this Pokémon lose 1/8 (12.5%) of their maximum HP, rounded down.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After a successful contact-tagged damaging hit, use the defender's hit snapshot to deal ceil(attacker maximum HP/8), minimum 1, to the living attacker as indirect ability damage, even if this holder fainted. Resolve once per primary hit event independently of damage amount. Misses, zero-damage immunity, Long Reach, and damage-only chains do not trigger it. Magic Guard and shared indirect-damage protections may block retaliation; retaliation cannot generate contact reactions or recursive chains. No chance, duration, AP cost, or cooldown applies. The ceil amount follows current game rounding. Preview this separate HP consequence and finish the retaliation before KO/result settlement, preserving simultaneous-defeat handling when it defeats the attacker.

Name: Iron Fist
Description: Powers up punching moves.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add a conditional modifier to shared damage calculation for the move, type, target, and conditions described.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's punch-based attacks have their power multiplied by 1.2 (+20%).
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: Multiply the base power of the holder's damaging moves tagged punch by 1.2 before the ordinary damage formula. Qualification depends on explicit move metadata after contact overrides, not the name, animation, Physical category, or melee delivery; a non-contact punch still qualifies. Untagged moves and Status moves receive no bonus. Apply once for the entire move profile, including all eligible area recipients, and combine with distinct modifiers such as Tough Claws only when their separate conditions hold. The effect is continuous and supplies no stages, duration, AP discount, or extra attacks. Audit imported punch tags and use the same resolved power in previews, enemy scoring, suppression, and ability feedback.

Name: Justified
Description: When the Pokémon is hit by a Dark-type attack, its Attack stat is boosted by its sense of justice.
Proposed: PROPOSED: Add an incoming-hit hook; check the described move or damage condition, then apply its prevention, healing, or stat response.
Exact Description: This Pokémon's Attack is raised by 1 stage after it is damaged by a Dark-type move.
proposed game implementation(detailed): PROPOSED: After the holder survives actual HP damage from a resolved Dark-type attack, raise its Attack by 1 stage for five cycles. Use the move's final converted type, with 100% probability; a miss, absorption, immunity, indirect damage, or non-damaging Dark move grants nothing. Trigger once per primary hit event, refreshing that stat's expiry and adding up to +6 on repeated eligible hits. Damage-only chains follow the game's existing no-secondary-reaction policy and do not grant extra Justified triggers. Apply shared stage guards, Contrary, and suppression rules; the bonus never refunds AP or grants another Attack command.
